AI prompt settings now have explicit Save and Revert to Default buttons

highlights: Cmd/Ctrl+F search now works inside HTML previews and plugin panels
App recovers automatically if the main window config is missing or corrupted
File drops from Finder to File Browser now land on the correct panel on Retina displays
Plugin iframes no longer reload twice when pressing Cmd/Ctrl+R
Linux and Windows release builds no longer fail on macOS-only window APIs
UI freeze detector tracks main-thread stalls for diagnostics
Git Panel log now shows the full commit message body when you expand a commit
GitHub login requests fewer permissions (dropped unnecessary read:org scope)

Terminal recovers from WebView stalls in 1s instead of 5s

Native-feel smooth scrolling with momentum and a draggable scrollbar

highlights: Dictation preview now shows a live microphone meter so you can confirm your mic is picking up speech before transcription starts.
The status bar no longer crashes when the Claude usage badge rotates out at the moment it's being drawn.
Creating a branch based on a local branch whose name contains a slash (e.g. POC-0001/merge-radar) now works.
Agents stay marked busy through API connection-retry loops instead of falsely appearing idle between attempts.
CI auto-heal reaches the branch agent immediately on a failed job even while sibling jobs keep the workflow running.
Switching an MCP HTTP upstream from Bearer to OAuth now clears the old token and reconnects with the chosen method.
Saving settings no longer loses fields between panels or silently disables the Remote Access web server and global hotkey.
Restarting the remote HTTP server keeps stdio MCP clients like Claude connected with their tools instead of dropping to zero.
Multi-agent MCP orchestration is now far more reliable, with socket stalls, stale bindings, and blocking-wait races fixed.
Agent-to-agent messages now use bounded inboxes and never overwrite your typed input or leave ghost "busy" sessions behind.
Background work (Cargo builds, tests) keeps agents marked working instead of falsely reporting completion at a ready prompt.
Agent completion is now distinct from idle, with a separate task-level state so finished turns are reported accurately.
MCP-spawned agents accept an optional name that stays stable in terminal tabs across reconnects.
Codex and OpenCode spawning and message submission are now reliable, with correct model args and prompt placement.
Dev builds use a separate repository list, so running a dev instance no longer overwrites your installed app's repos.
Build Cleaner no longer rescans every repository after each reload, sharing one scan and reusing recent results.
Updated the entire dependency stack (Vite 8, Vitest 4, TypeScript 7, Tauri 2.11) for better security and performance.
Web Push now signs with P-256 directly, dropping a vulnerable RSA dependency and picking up the quick-xml security fix.
The Activity Dashboard now shows a ready agent as idle even when Codex keeps a background dev server alive.
Agent status rows no longer stick, flicker, or erase a visible choice prompt at turn boundaries.
Claude now recovers cleanly when an idle hook is missed after real turn activity.
MCP peer messages no longer create ghost turns or fail to wake an idle agent into a new turn.
Blocking MCP waits now honor their deadline (60s default, 300s max) instead of hitting a stray 10-second cutoff.
Spawned agents now return a durable task handle with a new `task` tool to poll status past the 5-minute wait ceiling, so long-running work survives a disconnect.
MCP `tools/call` works without a protocol session header — a plain curl against `POST /mcp` is now enough for actions that need no identity.
Agent tabs no longer flip falsely idle or falsely completed: Codex, Claude and Grok activity detection now tracks their current status rows, composers and background terminals.
Codex terminals no longer adopt another project's session, and heavy Codex streaming no longer stalls behind an unterminated synchronized update.
Grok can now call MCP tools proxied through TUICommander, which it previously discarded silently.
Saving part of the configuration no longer silently disables remote access, and a failed save no longer rotates vault-backed credentials.
F13–F20 can now be bound to shortcuts and the Global Hotkey on macOS, and the `tuic` CLI's session and agent commands now show real ids, names and status.
Fixed stuck SSH tunnels, ghost worktree branches in the sidebar, stacked Markdown viewer/editor panes, and directory traversal on absolute-path file endpoints.
tuic run starts a command in a fresh session, and tuic ls now prints short IDs plus --json for scripting.
tuic capture -n tails recent output, tuic status names sessions waiting on you, and targets match name prefixes case-insensitively.
tuic . opens a directory as a repository again, activating known repos silently and confirming new ones once.
tuic send only treats whole-token key names as keys, so text like "Enter the room" types correctly; arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown and C-<letter> are covered.
Fullscreen apps that print past the bottom of the window — gh run watch, long build monitors — now keep a scrollback you can actually scroll, isolated from your shell history.
Updating mdkb now reconnects to the new daemon instead of silently talking to the stale one.
Quiet dictation no longer types phantom subtitle credits like "Grazie." in any of the eleven supported languages.
The whole Rust workspace is now tested in make check and CI, covering 267 previously skipped tests.
pi is now a fully tracked agent: correct classification, busy/idle detection, and resume via `pi --continue`.
Completion chimes can be muted for MCP-spawned sessions via Settings > Notifications > Orchestration.
Grok tabs now go idle after a finished turn instead of staying busy forever (new composer layout plus scrollbar false positive).
Scrolled-off agent output stays in the mobile log instead of being silently dropped from history.
Renaming a file to a different case now works on macOS and Windows.
Notes survive a failed config load: a corrupt file is moved aside instead of being overwritten with an empty list.
Worktrees survive a rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert, or bisect, and removed worktrees now disappear from the sidebar.
Cmd+C copies text selected inside plugin dashboards and other panel iframes.
Agent wait and inbox now always return next_since, so a timeout no longer forces a full history reload
since is now optional on wait and inbox: omit it to resume from a server-side per-identity cursor, or pass 0 to replay
delivered_via_channel is gone from send responses; delivery_path names the actual route and is the single field to read
register now accepts replaces=<old_uuid> to hand a mailbox over to a new identity across MCP connections, with a warning when the old peer still owns a live terminal
The find shortcut re-focuses an already-open search bar in the terminal, code editor, diff, HTML preview and markdown
Orchestrator inbox wakes retry at most once per unread group instead of looping every five seconds forever
Creating a worktree opens it in its own terminal and leaves a running agent on its real branch and directory
Managed Codex peers now inherit TUIC_SESSION through the MCP entry, so their first agent send works without manual registration
Queue follow-up commands with Shift+Ctrl+Enter — they run at the next idle window instead of interrupting the agent.
Toasts are now mirrored into a Messages section in the toolbar bell, so you can read them after they fade.
Agents can request a distinct Attention sound on MCP toasts, on both desktop and browser clients.
Cleaning up a merged worktree now confirms before discarding uncommitted work, and archiving really keeps the files.
A tab no longer stays badged "question" after you answer with a bare Enter or after a generic notification.
MCP bridge config is written only for agents you actually have installed, and unparsable configs are never overwritten.
agent detect now reports every agent TUIC can launch, and only the ones present on your machine.
Re-authorizing an HTTP MCP upstream takes effect on the next attempt, and Manage in Settings lands on the MCP block.
Queued Compose commands are now listed in delivery order, and you can delete a single one without clearing the rest.
The toolbar bell now shows the newest notification first instead of burying it under older history.
`tuic agent send` now reaches registered peers that have no terminal of their own, matching the MCP send tool.
A message that nothing will surface now reports "Buffered for <peer> (inbox_only)" instead of falsely claiming delivery.
`tuic agent type` splits text and Enter as separate writes, so raw-mode TUIs receive the input instead of leaving it as prefill.
Vague OSC 777 notifications no longer latch a permanent awaiting-input badge; only explicit permission prompts stay confident.
Confirmation prompts from agents now reach the desktop, every browser tab, and the phone with push, first answer wins.
Installing the MCP bridge preserves your Zed, VS Code, and opencode settings byte-for-byte, with backups and a remove-all button.
Browser and PWA clients gain working AI chat history, Command Palette, plugin watcher matches, and reliable event delivery.
Agent state is more accurate: idle root shells, awaiting-input, and stuck badges no longer misreport work.
Git, search, dictation, and Build Cleaner panels now show current state instead of results from before your last action.
Long AI answers and phone terminal views stay responsive as output grows, rendering only what changed.
Session history, repository edits, and terminal command blocks survive concurrent saves, restarts, and multi-window use.
Terminal links with trailing punctuation open correctly, and copying Claude output no longer pastes its quote gutter.
A tab parked in an unregistered repo now names the missing directory and offers a one-click Register to move it home.
Repository lists stay in sync across desktop, browser and phone, so one window's save no longer undoes another's.
Repository settings no longer stop saving because two windows computed different diff counts at the same moment.
Per-repository settings like base branch, setup script and worktree toggle now survive a restart.
A cd inside a terminal no longer moves an owned tab to another repo; only unowned parked tabs follow it.
Agent toasts show which repo they came from, and clicking one moves the sidebar, branch, pane and focus there.
An agent that quotes a menu on screen no longer marks its own tab as waiting for you.
Worktrees created by an agent now offer a Switch toast that waits in the bell instead of a blocking modal.
Suspend an idle terminal tab to free memory and CPU, then resume its agent later, even after a restart.
Hands-free voice conversations work on desktop and in the browser, with spoken replies in six languages.
Native plans, stories and workflow runs let you track, review and integrate agent work inside the app.
AI Chat keeps one conversation across repositories, with image paste, draft parking and conversation recovery.
Remote machines deploy and update themselves over SSH, stream compressed output and accept dropped files.
On mobile you can answer Claude and Codex questions, get push alerts, browse files and search sessions.
Desktop alerts, a Progress Flow view and reorganized Settings with an expert mode make work easier to follow.
The HTTP API now requires credentials even locally, and several MCP tool actions were renamed or removed.
Project Progress records what agents actually accomplished, in a per-project panel you can read after being away.
Progress exports a deterministic progress.md, previewed before it is written and never overwriting a hand edit.
Workspace creation is now linked Git worktrees only, still arriving warm through copy-on-write of ignored directories.
Claude and Codex status signals are launch-scoped and on by default, leaving your global configuration untouched.
Plan Tracker and Stories Ticker ship as ordinary plugins, so both can be updated or removed independently.
An AI stream now reaches a detached panel instead of rendering nowhere once the docked terminal unmounts.
The MCP session and peer payloads dropped the fields that restated each other, and is_caller marks the caller's own tab.
Windows is exercised by the suite now, fixing tilde expansion, plugin ZIP installs, child environment inheritance and the progress store there.
The TLS stack takes rustls 0.23.45 for RUSTSEC-2026-0285, covering remote access, the relay and tunnel HTTPS calls.
Agents can now interrupt a busy Claude, Codex or ego session with urgent mail that is delivered once the agent is idle.
Abandoned shells show how long they have been idle, and an optional setting closes them after a set number of hours.
Sidebar session menus can copy a session's alias, ID or live process ID.
Claude, Codex, Grok and ego questions and approvals are detected more reliably, with correct answer buttons everywhere.
Mobile gains Codex and Grok Chat views, a New Session list of installed agents, and fixes to layout and safe areas.
Sidebar Git status, worktree lists and plugin reloads do much less repeated disk work, so the app stays light on resources.
macOS no longer puts TUICommander into App Nap, so hidden windows keep updating without long stalls.
BREAKING: MCP per-tool switches are now capability groups and old tool aliases are gone, so reconnect clients after updating.
Stories now have an Edit form, append-only notes, detailed history, and status and type filters with a Kanban view.
You can edit plans in place with Save and Cancel, and you can detach Plans and Stories into a separate window.
Stories move to QA by themselves when only manual checks remain, so human checks stay apart from development work.
Mobile now shows ego question controls, session quota and cost, faster Progress lists, and no gap below the iOS composer.
Terminal Chat opens faster, stays readable in dark and light themes, and hides agent-mail wake notices.
Any agent connected through MCP can now send Telegram notifications, and Settings now shows the MCP call audit.
Orphan cleanup now skips detached and temporary worktrees, and Delete clearly says that the workspace is archived.
Stopped MCP servers restart automatically, and Tailscale HTTPS status and certificates now work reliably on macOS.
Manage Ideas from the planner API, the CLI and the workflow MCP tool, and the Ideas panel stays in sync.
Headless tuic-remote now serves GitHub poller controls, repository status, PRs and issues with existing authentication.
Final agent API failures from Claude, Codex and ego now stay red after the agent goes idle or a retry fails.
Mute sounds and OS notifications from agent-spawned sessions while keeping urgent cards visible.
Queued commands and replies reach idle agents waiting on progress reports without bypassing native dialogs.
Mobile shows Working, Idle and Awaiting counts, keeps CLI output pinned during resizes and recovers from outages.
Markdown reviews default to the agent that opened the document, and comment actions no longer cover list content.
Buttons, switches, sliders and settings controls share consistent desktop sizes and 44px mobile touch targets.
